notes.detailedSummary: On a fixed smooth compact Kähler manifold, the supplied whole P19.1 theorem gives actual model recovery. Comparing zero-start and singular-start maximal rays gives constant ordered d1 distance A_j. Applying the constant-invariant mixed estimate to normalized energy first restores means and bounds the contracted-energy difference by C[A_j+A_j^q(t+A_j+1)^(1-q)]. Fixed PL-test integrals require no mean-restoration term. Per-index entropy classification, convex Mabuchi secants and fixed-test Gibbs lower bounds then prove every joint index/time entropy limit. This concerns entropy divided by time, not fixed-time entropy or prescribed singularity endpoints.
notes.text:
Fix a connected smooth compact Kähler manifold (X,omega), dimension n>=1, alpha=[omega], V=integral omega^n and mu0=omega^n/V. Use dd^c=i/(2pi), t=-log|tau|^2, logarithm-square divisor coefficients, probability energy E(0)=0 and full probability entropy H. Retain the original X^beth over trivially valued C, including semivaluation supports.

The sole substantial theorem grant used is the whole supplied P19.1 mathematical theorem: actual maximal rays r(w,phi) exist for w in E1 and phi in E1_NA, are ordered in both arguments, and satisfy E(r_t)=E(w)+tE_alpha(phi). A maximal ray with a finite-entropy slice has entropy slope H_alpha(phi). Finite H_alpha(phi) admits actual smooth equivariant relatively Kähler models eta_j converging strongly with recovered discrepancy entropy. Its calibrated mixed slopes and log-canonical tests retain this fixed-manifold signature. No endpoint theorem is granted.

Take these models. Suppose either w is fixed with H(w)<infinity, or w_j->w in analytic d1 with sup_j H(w_j)<infinity. Normalize sup w_j=0 and write A_j=-E(w_j), a_j=r(0,eta_j), b_j=r(w_j,eta_j). Then A_j is bounded, a_j>=b_j and d1(a_j(t),b_j(t))=A_j. For m(u)=integral u dmu0 and J(u)=m(u)-E(u), one has J(a_j(t))<=Ct and J(b_j(t))<=J(a_j(t))+A_j.

The primary MP Lemma5.3.2, arXiv:2409.06221v2, bounds mixed-pairing differences of mean-zero E1 slots by C epsilon^q R^(1-q), q=2^-n. Here epsilon bounds constant-invariant relative J distances and R bounds the slots’ J values plus the fixed supremum-minus-mean constant. Its complete decreasing-continuity proof and pertinent fixed-test argument in Theorem5.3.4 were read. Relative J is bounded by ordered d1 and is invariant under separate constant changes. It is not legitimate to assume that d1 itself is invariant under separate mean subtraction.

Apply this estimate to normalized ENERGY first. It gives |E(a_j^0)-E(b_j^0)|<=C A_j^q(t+A_j+1)^(1-q). Since E(a_j)-E(b_j)=A_j, the mean difference is bounded by A_j plus this error. Restoring means in the fixed contracted energies gives
|G(a_j(t))-G(b_j(t))|<=C[A_j+A_j^q(t+A_j+1)^(1-q)].
For a fixed compatible divisor test Psi, the integral difference is bounded by C_Psi A_j^q(t+A_j+1)^(1-q), without a mean-restoration term: ray-slot constants integrate dd^c Psi against a closed product to zero, and test constants cancel between probability measures. The forms and test model are fixed before either limit. MP’s source convention uses background 2omega, potentials u_(2s), datum 2phi in class 2alpha, followed by t=2s.

For each j, the supplied entropy classification applies to b_j at its finite-entropy initial slice. Its entropy slope is h_j=H_alpha(eta_j); its contracted slope is g_j=G_alpha(eta_j). BDL’s Theorem4.7, published Geometry & Topology21 (2017), gives convex lower-semicontinuous Mabuchi M=H+G on canonical E1 weak geodesics. Every finite secant is bounded by its finite recession slope, hence M(b_j(t))<=M(w_j)+t(h_j+g_j). A finite-time infinite value would contradict that finite slope. The intercepts are uniformly bounded.

For zero starts, use the genuine common upper maximal ray with datum max(eta_j,phi). Strong fixed-measure integrability and the supporting energy inequality give B_j=2E_alpha(max(eta_j,phi))-E_alpha(eta_j)-E_alpha(phi)->0 and d1(a_j(t),r(0,phi)_t)<=tB_j. The normalized-energy-first estimate yields the joint limit G(a_j(t))/t->G_alpha(phi). The bounded A_j estimate transfers it to b_j. The convex bound therefore gives the joint entropy limsup at most H_alpha(phi).

For the liminf, first fix one SNC model Y. Its granted calibrated log-canonical volume has Psi_t=log(mu_Y,t/mu0), PL test A_X composed with retraction, and integral mu_Y,t<=C_Y(1+t)^n, retaining every central multiplicity. Gibbs’ inequality gives H(b_j(t))>=integral Psi_t MA(b_j(t))-log C_Y-n log(1+t). Replace b_j by a_j with an error divided by time tending uniformly to zero, then replace a_j by the target with error C_Y B_j^q. The calibrated slope gives the fixed discrepancy-test integral. Only after the joint liminf take the directed supremum over fixed SNC tests. This proves H(r(w_j,eta_j)_t)/t->H_alpha(phi) along every j,t->infinity.

BDL Lemma3.1 with f=0 provides genuine smooth initial regularizers converging in d1 with converging entropy for every finite-entropy E1 start. Its density truncation, smoothing, smooth MA solution and uniqueness proof was checked in the primary text. This controls initial entropy; it does not prove entropy continuity at every later fixed time. Nor does constant ray distance prove relative P-envelope preservation.

The complete proof is P19.2-argument.md Section4 and standalone P19.2-paper.tex. Exact source applications are in source-application-ledger.json. Their actual rays have endpoint w_c, raw mass1-c and a uniform analytic entropy remainder in[-2,0]. Choosing c_j=1-1/j and discrepancy moment r_j->0 gives strong uniform datum convergence to0 and eventual exact recovery of every fixed lambda<0, while endpoint mass is1/j and its d_S distance from0 tends to1/2. notes.text:
Use P1, omega=dd^c log(1+|z|^2), integral omega=1, and the conventions in n1.

Blow up (z,tau)=(0,0), then repeatedly the newest exceptional component’s intersection with the strict central component. After m blowups the fan rays are (1,i), i=1,...,m, with adjacent determinants one. The resulting surface is smooth, projective and equivariant. Its actual central fiber is B=F0+sum_i i F_i, with incidence F0,Fm,...,F1. Self-intersections are F0^2=-m, F_i^2=-2 for i<m and F_m^2=-1.

For positive rational a_i of sum c<1, set d_i=-sum_k a_k min(1,i/k), D=sum_i d_i F_i and L=p_z^*O(1)+D. A common denominator produces a genuine invertible sheaf. Chain intersection gives L.F0=1-c and L.F_i=a_i/i, all strictly positive. Stacks0B5Y says that an invertible sheaf on a proper scheme of dimension<=1 is ample exactly when every one-dimensional component degree is positive. Supplied09MS preserves ampleness through nilpotent thickening; freshly read0D2S supplies relative ampleness near an ample proper fiber. These apply to the actual nonreduced fiber, with all multiplicities retained. An auxiliary positive base twist supplies a global Kähler representative without changing the normalized relative divisor.

Set S_i=sum_{k<=i}a_k, v(x)=1/i on (S_(i-1),S_i), g(x)=integral_x^c v on [0,c] and zero beyond, r=sum_i a_i/i, and F(x)=x log x+(1-x)log(1-x). Define q_t(rho)=max_(0<=x<=1)[x rho-F(x)-t g(x)] and u_t=q_t(log|z|^2)-log(1+|z|^2). Then u_0=0 and -rt<=u_t<=0.

Actual divisor compatibility follows by omitting F to obtain h, with h<=q<=h+log2. The support maximum includes x=0, every node S_i and x=1. Clearing denominators gives monomials z^(M S_i) tau^(M g(S_i)) and z^M. On the cone between (1,k),(1,k+1), node S_k minimizes both ray orders. Every quotient by that generator has two nonnegative integral exponents in the smooth chart, and the chosen quotient is one. The first cone uses x=0 and the last uses x=c. Thus the ideal is actually invertible; its coefficient on F_k is M min_x(x+k g(x))=-M d_k. The pure-tau node gives a unit off the central fiber, while z^M gives a unit in the infinity frame. Removing the factor proves U+log|s_D|^2=O(1).

Its datum is phi(s ord0)=-sum_i a_i min(s,1/i) on the zero branch and zero elsewhere. At the supported zero semivaluation it equals-r. Multiplicity times degree gives MA_alpha(phi)=(1-c)delta_trivial+sum_i a_i delta_(ord0/i). The canonical coefficient kappa_i=i and b_i=i give over-X discrepancy1/i, hence H_alpha(phi)=r. Intersection energy is E_alpha(phi)=D^2/2=-1/2 sum_(i,k)a_i a_k min(1/i,1/k)=-integral g.

Convex time minimization gives Legendre levels0 for lambda<=-r; w_b for-r<lambda<0 where g(b)=-lambda; w_c at lambda0; and-infinity above0. Here w_b=b log|z|^2-F(b)-log(1+|z|^2) inside |z|^2<=b/(1-b), and0 outside. Its curvature is b delta0 plus omega outside that disk, with no circle atom; its raw non-pluripolar mass is1-b. For any rooftop competitor h<=0,h<=w_b+C, the local weight Q=h+log(1+|z|^2) has an atom at least b. Thus Q-b log|z|^2 extends subharmonically across0. Its boundary bound and the maximum principle force h<=w_b. This proves P[w_b]=w_b, including the endpoint.

The computed curve is decreasing, parameter-concave, upper semicontinuous and bounded with every nontrivial level P-model. The exact analytic DZ arXiv:2208.08324v4 Theorem3.7(ii), whose Perron replacement proof was read, identifies its inverse transform as the actual bounded weak ray from0. Its radial probability is dx, its time derivative is-g(x), and E(u_t)=t E_alpha(phi). Equality of actual and datum energy slopes gives maximality for the actual usual datum by the supplied theorem’s energy-defect criterion.

On (S_(i-1),S_i), the density against omega is exp(t/i)(1-x+exp(-t/i)x)^2; beyond c it is1. First derivatives match at all interfaces. Consequently H(u_t)=tr+2 sum_i integral_(S_(i-1))^S_i log(1-x+exp(-t/i)x) dx, with remainder in[-2,0], uniformly in models and time.

Now take m=j>=2, a_i=j^-3 for i<j, and a_j=1-1/j-(j-1)j^-3. Then c_j=1-1/j and r_j=a_j/j+j^-3 sum_(i<j)1/i->0. All degrees remain positive. Sup datum and cutoff are exactly0; ||phi_j||=r_j and energy and discrepancy entropy tend to0. Every joint j,t->infinity has H(u_j(t))/t->0. Every fixed lambda<0 eventually has level0 exactly. Nevertheless the endpoint is w_(1-1/j), with mass1/j, pole coefficient1-1/j and d_S distance (1-1/j)/2 from the target endpoint0. DDNL arXiv:1909.00839 Lemma3.4, transported to probability energy, gives this ordered distance. Changing to moving cutoffs cannot repair the example because every cutoff is already0.

This proves a recovery-to-endpoint implication failure. It does not prove nonexistence: the constant trivial model sequence preserves the target-zero endpoint exactly. Positive real coefficients also give actual relatively Kähler cohomological models by a small rational-vertex positivity simplex. Their compatibility uses real weighted logarithms of actual invertible ideals (z^i,tau), rather than nonexistent fractional holomorphic monomials.

notes.summary: New restricted constructive result: finite actual models preserve an infinite P1 chain’s endpoint, pole and mass exactly, with exact entropy and eventual exact recovery of each fixed interior envelope. The added chain and positive-endpoint hypotheses leave full P19.2 open.
notes.detailedSummary: For positive real a_i with sum c in(0,1), speeds1/i and entropy r=sum a_i/i, keep a finite prefix and replace the tail by finitely many strictly positive weights with the same tail mass and discrepancy moment. Two end weights plus small positive intermediate weights solve these constraints while retaining positivity on every actual central component. The finite speed functions agree on the retained prefix and differ uniformly by at most T/m. Their actual model data converge uniformly and strongly, retain H_alpha=r and endpoint w_c at every index, and eventually recover each fixed interior P envelope and pole exactly. Entire-level d_S error is at most T/2 and raw-mass error at most T. This is a genuine construction for specified one-dimensional chain data with initial0 and a positive endpoint, using real cohomological models.
notes.text:
The actual finite-chain model, ray and P-envelope lemma, including its real-coefficient extension, is established in n2. Here is an endpoint-preserving construction for a specified infinite-support input in that class.

Fix positive real a_i for every i>=1 with c=sum_i a_i in(0,1). On P1 set S_i=sum_(k<=i)a_k, v(x)=1/i on (S_(i-1),S_i), g(x)=integral_x^c v and zero beyond c, and r=sum_i a_i/i. The target datum is phi(s ord0)=-sum_i a_i min(s,1/i), zero on other branches, with supported zero value-r.

For each m retain all weights i<m. Let T=sum_(i>=m)a_i and R=sum_(i>=m)a_i/i. Strict infinite positivity gives0<R/T<1/m. Choose finite N>m with1/N<R/T. Give every intermediate index m<i<N a sufficiently small positive weight epsilon. Set T'=T-epsilon(N-m-1), R'=R-epsilon sum_(m<i<N)1/i, retaining T'>0 and1/N<R'/T'<1/m. Put tilde a_m=(R'-T'/N)/(1/m-1/N) and tilde a_N=T'-tilde a_m. Both are strictly positive. Together with the retained prefix and intermediate weights, these finite coefficients have exactly total mass c and discrepancy moment r, and every index1,...,N is positive.

Apply n2’s real finite-chain construction. Each approximant is an actual smooth equivariant relatively Kähler cohomological model with positive degree on every central component. It need not be a rational bundle if the prescribed real moments are irrational.

Its speed g_m agrees with g on [0,S_(m-1)] because both the prefix speeds and remaining integral R agree exactly. Both vanish beyond c, and tail speeds are at most1/m, hence ||g_m-g||<=T/m->0. Convex duality bounds the datum difference by this norm at every finite zero-branch valuation. Both supported values are exactly-r and other branches are0, so convergence is uniform on the original full X^beth.

The bounded psh and finite-energy foundations retained in the whole supplied P19.1 theorem give uniform energy and strong convergence. The explicit energies tend to-integral g. The model measures agree on the retained prefix and at the trivial atom of mass1-c; remaining parts each have mass T, so their total variation distance to nu=(1-c)delta_trivial+sum_i a_i delta_(ord0/i) is at most2T. Strong MA continuity identifies MA_alpha(phi)=nu. Its discrepancy integral is r, and every approximant has exactly that entropy.

The convex maximization gives ||u_m(t)-u(t)||<=t||g_m-g||, uniformly on bounded time intervals. The supplied actual maximal-ray continuity identifies this limit with r(0,phi); equivalently its directly computed bounded P-model test curve satisfies the analytic correspondence used in n2. Thus the datum is not merely assigned to an unrelated ray.

The levels are0 below-r, w_b for g(b)=-lambda, w_c at0 and-infinity above0. The endpoint w_c is EXACTLY identical at every index, preserving its P envelope, polar set{0}, logarithm-square pole coefficient c and raw mass1-c. For each fixed-r<lambda<0 its inverse b<c eventually lies below S_(m-1), where g_m=g. That level is eventually the same potential w_b pointwise, hence the same envelope, pole and all mixed raw masses. This is eventual exactness separately at each fixed parameter, rather than equality of an entire continuum at every finite index.

For remaining levels, both inverse values lie in [S_(m-1),c] and differ by at most T. The ordered formula in n2 gives uniform d_S error at most T/2 over lambda<=0 and uniform raw-mass error at most T. In dimension one these include all mixed level masses. Every finite approximant has entropy tr plus a remainder in[-2,0], giving every joint index/time limit r. The target obeys the same countable-interval density formula; its absolute entropy remainder is bounded by2 integral_0^c -log(1-x)dx<=2. There is no extra curvature at the accumulating boundary c: the dual derivative of strictly convex F+t g is continuous and its maximizing values tend to c.

This is a genuine constructive approximation for the stated infinite-chain input. It assumes P1, one chain with speeds1/i, initial0, real cohomological models and positive endpoint c<1. These additional hypotheses are not imposed to claim closure of original P19.2. Arbitrary log-discrepancy P signatures, general zero-mass endpoints, singular relative starts and exact indexwise continuum preservation remain unresolved.

notes.text:
Use the actual maximal-ray order and energy premises stated in n1 and the same operator, time, carrier and probability conventions.

For bounded starts there is a complete preservation statement. If-C<=w<=0, then r(0,phi)_t-C<=r(w,phi)_t<=r(0,phi)_t. Legendre infima satisfy the same inequalities. Bounded singularity errors leave P_omega[.] unchanged, so all absolute P ceilings agree, including endpoints, and identically -infinity levels agree. Exact polar sets agree. DDNL arXiv:1705.05796v3 Theorem2.4 gives mixed non-pluripolar mass monotonicity for ordered singularity types in smooth pseudoeffective forms; applying both orders gives equality of all mixed raw masses. Its complete primary truncation proof was read. The levels themselves need not be equal functions.

For a full-mass unbounded start, blanket zero-mass endpoint invariance is false. Near infinity put zeta=1/z, rho=log|zeta|^2, delta=1/3, rho_B=-log2, C=1-delta-F(delta), with F(x)=x log x+(1-x)log(1-x). Define Q=-(-rho)^(1/3)+C for rho<=-1; Q=delta rho-F(delta) for-1<=rho<=rho_B; Q=log(1+exp rho) afterwards. Set w=Q-log(1+exp rho). Values and first derivatives match. Inner derivatives are Q'=(1/3)(-rho)^(-2/3) and Q''=(2/9)(-rho)^(-5/3), positive and joining a convex tangent and Fubini–Study. Hence w is global omega-psh, nonpositive, supremum0, and singular exactly at infinity.

There is no polar atom because Q'(-infinity)=0; Q'(+infinity)=1 gives full non-pluripolar mass1. Its energy tail is bounded by integral_1^infinity L^(1/3)L^(-5/3)dL, finite, and its reference integral is finite by exponential decay. Thus w belongs to E1. Its initial entropy is infinite: density f=(2/9)L^(-5/3)/p'(-L), p'(rho)=exp(rho)/(1+exp(rho))^2, has log f>=L/2 eventually, so the entropy tail dominates the divergent integral L^(-2/3)dL.

Take the boundary nef datum phi(s ord0)=-min(s,1), zero elsewhere. The supplied calibration gives E_alpha(phi)=-1/2, H_alpha(phi)=1 and zero-start ray a_t=log((|z|^2+exp(-t))/(1+|z|^2)). Its endpoint w1=log|z|^2-log(1+|z|^2) has ordinary curvature delta0 and raw mass0. It is P-model directly: every rooftop competitor below w1+C has an atom at least1 at0, hence its entire curvature is delta0 and it equals w1 plus a constant; the obstacle0 bounds that constant by0. No positive-mass envelope theorem is used.

Let b=r(w,phi). The stationary ray w_t=w has actual datum0: cube-root logarithmic growth has generic divisorial coefficient0 on every modification. It is an actual constant E1 weak ray of energy slope0, hence maximal for datum0 by the granted energy-defect criterion. Order gives b_t<=a_t and b_t<=w. The convex time functions bounded above by w are nonincreasing. Thus h=inf_t b_t is either omega-psh or identically -infinity. If nontrivial, h<=w1 forces a curvature atom at least1 at0, hence total curvature delta0 and h=w1+constant. This is finite at infinity, contradicting h<=w there. Therefore chi_b(0) is identically -infinity, while chi_a(0)=w1 is nontrivial. Ordered energy gives d1(a_t,b_t)=-E(w) for every t. Both endpoint masses are zero, but their P data differ.

This start has infinite entropy and the target is boundary nef. It is not a counterexample to finite-initial-entropy approximation or to existence in unchanged P19.2. General unbounded finite-entropy-start P-level invariance remains unproved here.

The primary Darvas–Zhang arXiv:2509.15173v2 definition and pertinent proofs were read: formula(11), Section9 and complete Theorem10.1. The log-discrepancy model is L_beta=L+beta^-1(K_rel+B_red-B), beta rational>1. Its datum is P_alpha(phi_L+beta^-1 A_X composed with retraction), rather than the PL obstacle in general; the bundle need not be relatively semiample. Theorem10.1 assumes a polarized manifold and an initial-zero E1 ray with finite radial entropy. It gives smooth log-discrepancy-model rays converging in chordal distance and radial entropy. Its resolution-independence, multiplicity-retaining integrability and replacement proof asserts no prescribed endpoint or exact-pole conclusion. It is used as a scope comparison, not an endpoint or transcendental grant.
